source_comparison: Go pkg/planner/core/stats.go::deriveStats4DataSource returns retained StatsInfo, consumes compiled PushedDownConds, fills paths, and derives one DataSource estimate.

Rust driver/join_reorder.rs::emit -> table_selectivity and driver/access.rs::commit_fast_path_source independently call AST selectivity. driver.rs still requests the row model for aggregates and DISTINCT before final single-table access planning.

access_cost.rs::selectivity_of_conjuncts_with_path_context compiles each AST condition anew. Fresh candidate has 1.083 sampled seconds under this rewrite and 0.362 under expression cloning (overlapping categories). Total selectivity share rises from 0.918% to 3.517%; this localizes added cost but is not an isolated causal throughput measurement.

Go expression.go::extractBinaryOpItems copies expression interfaces; Rust expr_util/normal_form.rs::split_normal_form_items clones expression trees. Go explicit ScalarFunction.Clone remains a distinct operation; do not globally equate copying an expression reference with semantic cloning.
compiled_owner_followup.next_root_change: Retain compiled predicates and the DataSource statistics they produce across row-model and physical-access consumers; then retain that plan through prepared execution. Preserve actual column identities, pushed versus root conditions, partition statistics and diagnostic timing. Do not add an AST-value cache, warning deduplication, or an aggregate-specific shortcut.
compiled_owner_followup.qualification: Candidate medians regress 1.91% at one client and 3.53% at eight. The nominal 2.24% gain at 32 is not accepted: broad drift and two of three matched pairs are negative. Go request batches are larger, but throughput is not consistently higher. Background desktop CPU is visible; this is not an isolated host.

source_comparison.batch_admission: Both collect on a shared queue before connection rotation. Go conn_batch.go conditionally waits and yields after the ready drain using the standard 100us adaptive policy. Rust transport_runtime/batching.rs immediately drains ready same-address commands, bounded by 128 and lifecycle barriers. Larger Go batches do not prove a causal throughput advantage; prior adaptive-wait Rust trials regressed.
source_comparison.timestamp_policy: Go common_plans.go IsPointGetWithPKOrUniqueKeyByAutoCommit, including the exact running revision, refuses index double reads and incomplete clustered keys. Rust classifiers incorrectly treated cached IndexPrefix and ClusteredPrefix plans as AutocommitPointGet; regression work follows these measurements.
